extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and patent agents drafting Indian patent applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing provisional and complete patent specifications, drawings, claims, and abstracts for Indian patent applications (including divisional, addition, and PCT-related matters). Covers content requirements, drafting style, formalities, and claim-clarity principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent of Addition: expiry and independence
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent of addition expires along with the main patent unless it is made independent according to the provisions in S.54.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Complete Specification for a patent of addition must include specific reference to the number of the main patent or its application and a definite statement that the invention comprises an improvement in, or a modification of, the invention claimed in the specification of the main patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional application rules
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application claims more than one invention the applicant may, on request or to meet an official objection, divide the application and file two or more applications (divisional applications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority date for divisional applications is the same as the parent (ante-dating). The complete specification of a divisional must not include matter not in substance disclosed in the first application and must reference the parent application in the body of the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form 2 and first-page formalities
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisional/complete specification must be submitted in Form 2. The first page should contain the title, name/address/nationality of each applicant, and a preamble to the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete description should start from the second page followed by date and signature. Claims follow the description and an abstract should be included on the next page after the date and signature. Drawings, if any, can be attached thereafter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional specification: nature and required content
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional specification is not a rough draft; it is a permanent independent document that should contain the title and description and start with the prescribed preamble.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims need not be included. After the preamble set forth the object of the invention, a statement of the principle or discovery underlying the invention, and a general statement of the actual invention. Include as much information as available; description should be adequate to identify the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete specification filing deadline after provisional
rubrics_metrics.description: An application filed with a provisional specification must be accompanied by a complete specification within twelve months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If complete specification is not filed within the specified time, the application will be abandoned unless the applicant requests postdating on or before expiry of 12 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on filing provisional specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisional specification cannot be filed for divisional, convention applications, or PCT applications designating India (Sec.16 or Sec.135).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Those applications must always be accompanied by a complete specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion between provisional and complete specifications and postdating
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant can convert a purported complete specification into a provisional specification by request within twelve months (S.9(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At any time before grant, a complete specification filed pursuant to an application with a provisional specification may be postdated to the filing date of the complete specification if requested; the provisional specification will then be treated as cancelled (S.9(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete Specification: definition and required preamble
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete Specification is a techno-legal document which fully and particularly describes the invention and the best method of performing it and should start with the prescribed preamble.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preamble wording: 'The following specification particularly describes the nature of this invention and the manner in which it is to be performed.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Page limits for complete specification
rubrics_metrics.description: The complete specification shall contain the required content in not more than 30 pages beyond which each page is chargeable as given in the first schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe page-count and fee rules per schedule when drafting longer specifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The title should give a fair indication of the art or industry to which the invention relates; be brief, precise, definite and free from fancy expressions or ambiguity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include the inventor’s name, the word ‘Patent’, words in other languages, the abbreviation 'etc.', or fancy trade-like names. Examples of acceptable titles are provided (e.g., 'Improved folding chair').

rubrics_metrics.name: Field of the invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Description should preferably begin with a short general statement showing the scope and indicating the subject matter to which the invention relates (e.g., 'This invention relates to ...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define in general terms and also describe with particularity by giving specified examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: State of the art / prior art disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Specification should indicate the status of technology in the field, reference relevant experiments, patents and pending patent applications, with emphasis on prior art relevant to the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When invention is an improvement, give a short statement of the closest prior art and clearly distinguish the invention from such closest prior art. If unaware of any prior art, state that.

rubrics_metrics.name: Object of the invention (problem & solution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specification should clearly bring out the necessity of the invention by stating the technical problems associated with existing technology and the solution provided by the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use clear object statements: 'The principal object of this invention is ...', 'Another object ...', etc., and show obvious differences between claimed invention and prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of invention (novel features)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a statement that sets forth the distinguishing novel features of the invention for which protection is desired, in verbatim complement to the claims and omnibus claim if needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical phrasing: 'Accordingly the invention provides an apparatus consisting of ... which is characterized in that ...'. Also state other aspects/processes if any.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed description sufficient for skilled person
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed description (with reference to drawings) must give a complete picture and sufficiently describe improvements/modifications to enable an average person skilled in the art to perform the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include examples and drawings where helpful; give a brief description of drawings before details. For chemical inventions supply sufficient examples. Describe mode of operation and function of parts, not just a parts list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biological material deposit and disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: If biological material cannot be completely described by words and is not publicly available, the material must be deposited in an authorized depository and the specification must state its characteristics and deposit details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose name/address of depository, date and number of deposit, source and geographical origin of biological material. For biotechnological inventions disclose source & geographical origin not later than filing and make reference in the specification within three months (sec 10(4)(d)(ii)[A] & Rule 13(8)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid vague or colloquial terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain vague terms should be avoided in the description (e.g., 'Special', 'design', 'suitable', 'etc.', 'whereby', 'if desired', 'and/or', 'customary methods', 'known methods').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terms in other languages must be accompanied by English equivalents. Avoid slang and colloquialisms. Use precise technical language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope/ambit of the invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Specification should set out areas of application, preferable uses, industrial applicability and advantages, and call for protection against duplication in related fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a non-limiting clause such as 'Although described with reference to specific embodiments, this description is not meant to be construed in a limiting sense' to allow modifications and alternate embodiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims define boundaries and must be precise
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims define the boundaries of the protection sought; what is not claimed is open to public use even if disclosed in the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims' object is to show concisely and accurately how much of what is described is sought to be protected. Each claim is evaluated on its own merit; one claim being objected does not invalidate others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims: single invention or linked group and basis in specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims shall relate to a single invention or a group of inventions linked so as to form a single inventive concept; they must be clear, succinct and fairly based on the matter disclosed in the specification (S.10(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure claims are fairly based on disclosure; terms used in claims must appear in or be clearly inferred from the description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited/insufficient claim forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain forms of statements are not to be regarded as claims (e.g., 'I claim to be the inventor', 'I claim a patent', claims that merely state novelty or assert advantages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use claims that merely illustrate efficiency or advantages (e.g., 'I claim this device is better and cheaper...'). Claims must define the invention, not laud it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product claims should not be mere property listings
rubrics_metrics.description: A product claimed merely by stating its properties (e.g., a lubricating oil defined only by specific gravity and boiling point) does not properly define the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims should identify structural or compositional features that define the invention, not only properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims referencing description/back-references
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims that merely refer back to the description (e.g., 'as described' or 'the invention described in the specification') are not sufficiently definitive unless the description explicitly states the characteristic features of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the description contains explicit statements of the features relied upon by such referential claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An abstract should be included after the claims to provide brief technical information, preferably within 150 words and starting on a fresh page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract must enable understanding of technical problem, solution and usefulness; include most relevant figure if necessary (especially engineering inventions). Abstract cannot be used to interpret scope of protection; Controller may amend abstract to better inform third parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings: format and referencing
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings referred to in the specification should be filed on standard A4 sheets in duplicate, preferably drawn in black indelible ink on durable paper with 2.5 cm margins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant's name at top-left, sheet numbers at top-right, signature at bottom-right with name. Use the same reference letters/numerals in description and figures; avoid descriptive matter on drawings except in certain cases; where space lacks, place letters outside and connect by fine lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: General drafting principles: good faith and clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: The Complete Specification must be framed with utmost good faith and must not contain false representation or description which would mislead the public; it must be as clear and concise as the subject admits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A specification that misleads or fails to disclose relevant information renders the patent invalid and liable to revocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intelligibility to a person skilled in the art
rubrics_metrics.description: The Complete Specification must be intelligible to an ordinary workman possessing ordinary skill and knowledge in that technical branch; it is not required to instruct a person wholly ignorant of the subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor technical level so a skilled practitioner can reproduce the invention from the disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best method disclosure requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Complete Specification must describe the best method known to the patentee of performing the invention and all knowledge relating thereto, including that acquired during the provisional protection period prior to filing the complete specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose practical working embodiments and any improvements known to applicant up to filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include modifications and variations
rubrics_metrics.description: An account of modifications and variations which fall within the scope of the claim may be included in the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mention alternative embodiments and optional features to widen effective protection and guide interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings should supplement detailed description
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed description should be supplemented by drawings in all cases where the invention can be illustrated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not insert drawings that require special printing preparation into the specification; make specific reference to drawings with a recommended phrasing: 'This invention is illustrated in the accompanying drawings, throughout which like reference letters indicate corresponding parts in the various figures.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe mode of operation and function, not just parts list
rubrics_metrics.description: It is insufficient to give merely a list of parts; the mode of operation of the apparatus and the function of its different parts must be described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how components interact and achieve the claimed technical effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent of Addition: specification content
rubrics_metrics.description: Specification for a Patent of Addition should contain at the beginning a definite statement that the invention comprises an improvement in or modification of the original invention and quote the serial number of the original application, plus a short statement of the earlier disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This helps establish relation to the main patent and clarifies scope of the addition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biotechnological inventions: source/geographical-origin disclosure timing
rubrics_metrics.description: For biotechnological inventions, disclose the source & geographical origin of the biological material in the specification not later than the date of filing in India and make a reference in the specification within three months (sec 10(4)(d)(ii)[A] & Rule 13(8)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure compliance with deposit and disclosure deadlines to avoid objections or defects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims: number, drafting order, and fees
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no restriction on the number of claims, but claims beyond 10 are chargeable. Good drafting typically begins with broad claims and proceeds to narrower claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use broad principal claims and narrower dependent claims specifying more details; multiple claims with varying scopes provide layered protection. Prefer one-sentence claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims should be specific, not vague or speculative
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim must be specific, not vague, ambiguous, speculative or hypothetical; avoid subjective terms like 'thin', 'strong', 'a major part', 'such as', 'when required', 'any'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each claim should be complete, covering the inventive feature and enough surrounding elements to put the invention in context; terms must be found in or inferred from the description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim structure: introductory phrase, body, and linking words
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim usually consists of an introductory phrase (category/purpose), the body (legal description), and a linking part joining the two.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common linking words/phrases include 'which comprises', 'including', 'consisting of', 'consisting essentially of'. Example claim structure is provided for guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent and dependent claims: roles and grouping
rubrics_metrics.description: The principal (first) claim should clearly define essential novel features of the preferred embodiment; subsidiary claims (dependent) claim alternative embodiments, optional features or linked inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dependent claims should be grouped with their independent claims. Independent claims may define alternate embodiments or inventions linked to principal claim (product/process/apparatus unity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Omnibus claim use
rubrics_metrics.description: An omnibus claim (e.g., 'An apparatus substantially as hereinabove described') may be added as the last claim to get integral protection only if a 'statement of invention' is incorporated in the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One or two application claims can precede the omnibus claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples for assessing claim clarity (vagueness, syntax, functional claiming)
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrative negative examples: (1) 'near-amorphous' is vague and unclear; (2) ambiguous syntax in specifying materials leads to multiple readings; (3) claiming by result (e.g., 'adapted to operate at temperatures down to 200 K') defines the object to be achieved rather than technical features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these examples to judge claim clarity: avoid vague adjectives, resolve syntactic ambiguity, and claim technical features rather than desired results where concrete features can be stated.
